question: Show the published IMD rice advice for Dibrugarh district, Assam.
answer:
From the Dibrugarh, Assam bulletin issued 2026-09-11, for rice:

Source guidance needs reconciliation: different passages contain permission and restriction wording for sowing. Their conditions and time scopes may differ. Both are retained below; no personal go/no-go conclusion has been made.

Bulletin context is incomplete: Likely impacts of weather warnings (General) — Empty, unreadable or oversized section; source review required. The crop excerpts do not establish complete bulletin guidance.

RICE · stage not stated · page 2:
“Considering suitable weather condition in the coming 5 days, go for second top dressing with Urea @ 4.5 kg per bigha in the medium and long duration semi dwarf varieties and 1.5 kg per bigha in medium and long duration tall varieties of sali rice which are at panicle initiation stage. In case of short duration (about 100 days) semi dwarf varieties the dose of urea for top dressing should be 9 kg per bigha.”

RICE · stage not stated · page 2:
“Since the weather condition has become favourable for the attack of swarming caterpillar in rice crop, farmers can go for traditionally controlling the pest by sweeping coconut ropes, dipped in kerosene oil across the rice crop, causing the caterpillars to fall into water and die, or place bird perches in the field. Periodically release ducks into the fields, which will in turn consume the larvae and reduce the pest infestation. To stop the movement of swarming caterpillars from one field to another, spray the bunds with Fipronil 5% SC @ 1ml/lit of water. In infested crop, spray Lambda-cyhalothrin 5 EC @ 1.5 ml/lit of water or Chlorantraniliprole 18.50% SC @ 1ml per 3 liters of water at 7 days interval during evening hours. Three sprayings are necessary to control the pest.”

RICE · stage not stated · page 2:
“Since there is possibility of getting light rainfall in the coming 5 days, repair the bunds in the paddy fields to conserve rain water. Maintain standing water of 5±2 cm depth in the field.”

Context from the same bulletin edition follows. These are separate source sections, not crop-specific matches or verified current official warnings. Printed warning dates and conditions are preserved; bulletin forecast dates do not extend their validity.

Forecast Summary: · page 1:
“The weather will remain partly cloudy with the possibilities of getting light rainfall in the coming 5 days. Daily maximum and minimum temperature for the ensuing 5 days is predicted to be around 35.7°C and 24.2°C respectively. Morning and afternoon relative humidity will be around 84% and 79% respectively. Wind will blow mainly from northeasterly direction at an average speed of around 2.0 kmph. Extended Range Weather Forecast: During the period from 13th September, 2026 to 19th September, 2026, the rainfall amount, maximum and minimum temperature will remain normal over Assam-Meghalaya Meteorological Subdivision.”

Weather Warnings (Valid Till 08:30 IST of the next day) · page 1:
“There is a probability of occurrence of heavy rain, thunderstorm and lightning in some isolated areas from 12th to 14th September, 2026”

Likely impacts of weather warnings on Agriculture and associated Agromet advisories · page 1:
“Provide mechanical support to the crops like banana, citrus, papaya etc. and make arrangements to drain out excess water from the fields. Harvest the matured vegetable and fruits and transfer it to a safer location. Transfer the seedlings of fruit crops, flower crops, vegetable crops etc. to a safer location. In case if the seedling cannot be transferred, make provisions for firm temporary sheds (made of bamboo and net or plastic).”

General Advisory: · page 2:
“Taking advantage of the suitable weather condition in the coming 5 days, farmers can continue their farm operations like, land preparation, sowing, transplanting, earthing up, application of fertilizers, spraying of pesticides, etc.”

SMS Advisory: · page 2:
“Burning of dried leaves mixed with dried chilli near the vegetable orchards will control the infestation of borers and suckers up to certain extent.”

Impact based advisories (General) · page 3:
“Follow any traffic advisories. • Avoid going to areas that face water logging problem often. • Avoid staying in landslide prone areas. • Take shelter during thunderstorm/lightning activities. • Provide mulch at the base of the crop to prevent soil and root damage. • Avoid working in the fields during thunderstorm/lightning period. • Postpone sowing of rice, jute, maize and vegetables; if already sown, avoid water stagnation in the field and cover the seeded area with natural mulching materials like straw, farm residues etc. • Be updated.”

These are original English source excerpts, including their conditions. The bulletin is district guidance; it has not been validated for your individual field.
